nodes.description: Owner address of the contract, set in constructor from msg.sender; receives a 5 finney fee cut on each registration.
Mapping address=>uint holding each player's pending withdrawal balance; credited in calcWinner/userRegister and drained in userWithdraw.
Signed integer round counter starting at 1; incremented every 4 registrations and used to index the participants array.
Number of players registered in the current round (0-3); controls winner calculation and round rollover.
Mapping int=>address[7] storing the players of each round; written on registration and by calcWinner when advancing winners.
Deployment constructor: sets owner = msg.sender, round = 1 and registered = 0.
View helper returning withdrawals[player] for an arbitrary address.
View helper returning the participant arrays of the previous and current round.
Public withdrawal of the caller's balance: requires withdrawals[msg.sender] > 0, zeroes it, then sends ether with msg.sender.transfer.
Payable registration entry point charging 105 finney; credits the owner, records the player, triggers calcWinner at slots 1 and 3, then advances registered/round counters.
Private function that pseudo-randomly picks the winner between two participants using blockhash and credits the reward to the winner's withdrawal balance.
Attacker-controlled caller address used as owner at deployment, as withdrawal key/recipient in userWithdraw, and as a participant in userRegister.
External low-level ether transfer msg.sender.transfer(amount) executed in userWithdraw after the balance is zeroed; the sink for reentrancy analysis.
Weak randomness source combining blockhash(block.number - 1) with participant addresses inside calcWinner to decide the winner.
Address parameter of publicGetBalance used to select the queried withdrawal entry.
First participant index parameter of calcWinner.
Second participant index parameter of calcWinner.
Destination slot index parameter of calcWinner for the advancing winner.
Reward amount (150 or 100 finney) credited to the winner's withdrawal balance in calcWinner.
Local variable amount in userWithdraw holding the caller's balance that is transferred out.
Local variable random in calcWinner derived from blockhash and participant addresses.

edges.reason: Constructor assigns the privileged owner role directly from the untrusted msg.sender, making ownership caller-dependent.
userRegister writes the untrusted msg.sender into participants[round][registered] to enroll the caller.
userWithdraw uses untrusted msg.sender as both the balance lookup key and the withdrawal validation subject.
Untrusted msg.sender is the direct recipient of the external transfer call in userWithdraw.
userWithdraw performs the external msg.sender.transfer(amount) call, the reentrancy sink of the contract.
userWithdraw reads and clears withdrawals[msg.sender] before the external transfer, coupling state with the reentrancy candidate.
Local variable amount is assigned from withdrawals[msg.sender] inside userWithdraw.
The local amount value flows into the external transfer call as the transferred quantity.
publicGetBalance reads the withdrawals mapping to return a player balance.
publicGetBalance indexes withdrawals with its player parameter.
Callers of publicGetBalance supply an arbitrary address, allowing anyone to query untrusted-selected accounts.
publicGetState reads participants[round-1] and participants[round] from the participants mapping.
userRegister conditionally invokes calcWinner when registered equals 1 or 3.
userRegister writes the caller into the participants mapping at the current round slot.
userRegister increments or resets the registered counter, a bounded unsigned counter manipulation.
userRegister increments the round counter on rollover, influencing later array indexing.
userRegister reads the owner state variable to address the 5 finney fee credit.
userRegister credits withdrawals[owner] with a fixed 5 finney amount (balance arithmetic).
calcWinner derives its winner decision from blockhash(block.number - 1) inside the unsafe random computation.
Local variable random is computed inside calcWinner from blockhash and participant addresses.
The local random value is consumed by the modulo check that selects the winner in the weak-randomness operation.
calcWinner reads and writes participants[round] to advance the winning participant.
calcWinner increases withdrawals[winner] by the reward amount, an unchecked balance accumulation.
calcWinner indexes participants with its first parameter.
calcWinner indexes participants with its second parameter.
calcWinner uses its winner parameter as the destination index for the advancing participant.
calcWinner adds its reward parameter to the winner's withdrawal balance.
publicGetState uses the round state variable to select which participant arrays to return.
calcWinner uses the current round state variable to index participants.

normalization_plan.reason: The parameter player only exists to index withdrawals inside publicGetBalance; it collapses into that core function node.
The parameter first is only meaningful as the participant index used by calcWinner and merges into that core function.
The parameter second is only meaningful as the participant index used by calcWinner and merges into that core function.
The parameter winner only selects the destination slot in calcWinner and merges into that core function.
The parameter reward only contributes the credited amount inside calcWinner and merges into that core function.
Local variable amount carries the caller balance straight into the external transfer, so it merges into the transfer unsafe_operation.
Local variable random is produced and consumed exclusively by the blockhash-based weak randomness computation, so it merges into that unsafe_operation.
